facts.fact: Agriculture and allied sectors contribute about 18% of GVA.
Agriculture employs about 45-46% of the workforce.
Over 58% of rural households depend on agriculture as their main livelihood.
Agriculture's share in GDP has been falling as services grew (structural transformation).
Agriculture covers about 43% of India's geographical area.
Agriculture GDP share was 19.9% in 2020-21 and 18.3% in 2022-23 (source text).
About 52% of cultivable land is rainfed.
Surplus farm labour whose removal would not cut output is disguised unemployment.
Kharif crops (rice, cotton, maize) are sown in June-July with the monsoon and harvested in September-October.
Rabi crops (wheat, gram, mustard) are sown in October-December and harvested in March-May.
Zaid crops (watermelon, cucumber, fodder) are short summer crops sown March-June.
Sericulture is silk production from silkworms; moriculture is growing mulberry.
Apiculture is beekeeping.
Viticulture is grape cultivation; vermiculture is rearing earthworms.
Pisciculture is the breeding and rearing of fish.
Aviculture is raising birds; arboriculture is cultivating trees and shrubs.
Floriculture is the cultivation of flowers and ornamental plants.
The First Plan gave 14% of its outlay to agriculture.
The Second Plan cut the farm allocation to 11.7%, focusing on industry.
The Third Plan introduced IADP and HYVP but saw negative farm growth (-0.73%).
The Sixth Plan saw the Second Green Revolution of 1983-84.
The Eighth Plan recorded the best Plan farm growth, 4.68%.
The Eleventh Plan missed its 4% agricultural growth target (3.6%).
Farm growth was 6.6% in 2017-18 and 3.5% in 2022-23.
Foodgrain output in 2025-26 (third advance estimates) was a record 376.56 million tonnes.
Wheat output in 2025-26 was about 121 million tonnes.
Horticulture output in 2025-26 was a record about 377.8 million tonnes, above foodgrains.
India became the world's largest rice producer in January 2026, overtaking China.
India is the world's largest exporter of rice (UPSC 2019).
India ranks first in total milk and total pulses.
India ranks first in jute production.
India ranks second in wheat, sugarcane, tea and cotton.
India ranks 3rd in eggs and 5th in meat.
West Bengal is the largest rice-producing state.
Uttar Pradesh is the largest wheat and sugarcane producer.
Gujarat leads in cotton and groundnut.
Rajasthan leads in mustard/rapeseed.
Madhya Pradesh leads in gram and soybean.
Assam leads tea, Karnataka coffee and Kerala natural rubber.
Uttar Pradesh is the largest milk-producing state.
The Green Revolution (post-1965) used HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers and assured irrigation.
M.S. Swaminathan led India's Green Revolution, drawing on Norman Borlaug's work.
Early Green Revolution gains were in wheat and rice in Punjab and Haryana.
Green Revolution drawbacks: groundwater and soil depletion, higher costs, regional imbalance.
C. Subramaniam was the Union Agriculture Minister behind the Green Revolution.
Norman Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
IR-8 was the HYV rice variety from IRRI.
IADP began in 1960-61 and the HYVP in 1966-67.
Under the US PL-480 (Food for Peace, 1954) programme India imported wheat before the Green Revolution.
The Bengal Famine of 1943 killed about 2-3 million people.
BGREI began in 2010-11 under the RKVY for eastern states.
BGREI states recorded 11.99% foodgrain growth in 2011-12.
The Second Green Revolution stresses eastern states, organic and contract farming and APMC amendments.
White Revolution = milk (Operation Flood, Kurien); Blue = fish; Yellow = oilseeds.
Pink Revolution = prawns/meat; Silver = eggs and poultry.
Golden Fibre Revolution = jute; Silver Fibre Revolution = cotton.
Golden Revolution = honey (source) / horticulture (many books).
Grey Revolution = fertilisers; Round Revolution = potato.
Red Revolution = meat and tomato; Brown Revolution = leather and cocoa.
The Yellow Revolution is linked to Sam Pitroda and the Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986).
The Evergreen Revolution is Swaminathan's idea of raising output without ecological harm.
The Rainbow Revolution denotes holistic development of agriculture with all allied revolutions.
The Rainbow Revolution was announced in 2000 aiming at 4% farm growth.
The Tricolour Revolution (PM Modi) covers Saffron (energy), White and Blue revolutions.
Operation Greens (Budget 2018) promotes tomato, onion and potato (TOP).
The Sweet Revolution promotes beekeeping under the National Beekeeping and Honey Mission.
Operation Flood began in 1970 under the NDDB (1965, Anand).
PMMSY (2020, ₹20,050 crore) drives the Blue Revolution.
Land reforms: abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reform, ceilings and consolidation.
The Bhoodan Movement (1951) was led by Acharya Vinoba Bhave.
V. Ramachandra Reddy made the first Bhoodan land donation.
Holdings: <1 ha marginal, 1-2 ha small, 2-4 ha semi-medium, 4-10 ha medium, >10 ha large.
India never nationalised all agricultural land.
'Small Farmer Large Field' means small farmers organising in groups to synchronise operations (UPSC 2023).
NITI Aayog drafted the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016.
NLRMP (2008) merged CLR and SRA&ULR; it is now the DILRMP.
Agriculture Census 2015-16: average holding 1.08 hectare; small and marginal about 86%.
The Kumarappa Committee (1949) recommended 'land to the tiller'.
MSP is recommended by the CACP.
MSP was introduced in 1965-66.
MSP was first announced for wheat (1966-67); CACP began as the APC in 1965, renamed 1985.
MSP is announced for 23 crops: 7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 4 commercial.
A2 = paid-out costs; A2+FL adds family labour; C2 adds imputed rent/interest on owned assets.
The Swaminathan Commission recommended MSP at least 50% above C2.
FCI buys foodgrains, NAFED pulses/oilseeds, CCI cotton.
Sugarcane FRP is approved by the CCEA (CACP recommends).
Agricultural markets are regulated under State APMC Acts (UPSC 2015).
Paddy (common) MSP for KMS 2026-27 is ₹2,441 per quintal.
Grade A paddy MSP for 2026-27 is ₹2,461.
Wheat MSP for RMS 2027-28 is ₹2,610 per quintal (+₹25).
Safflower got the highest MSP rise (₹675) for RMS 2027-28.
Sugarcane FRP for 2026-27 is ₹365 per quintal.
CACP also weighs terms of trade and inter-crop price parity.
UPSC 2018: MSP covers barley, finger millet, groundnut and sesamum, not areca nut, coffee or turmeric.
Niger is a Kharif oilseed with an MSP; some tribals use niger oil for cooking (UPSC 2023).
MSP, government trading, stockpiling and consumer subsidies all affect the price of rice (UPSC 2020).
Central Issue Price is the subsidised PDS issue price.
PM-AASHA (2018) comprises PSS, PDPS and PPPS.
PDPS pays farmers the gap between MSP and market price.
MSP is criticised for regional skew (Punjab, Haryana, MP) and encouraging water-guzzling paddy/wheat.
The Swaminathan NCF (2004-06) led to the National Policy for Farmers, 2007.
The Shanta Kumar Committee (2014) recommended restructuring FCI and found only about 6% of farmers sell at MSP.
The Ashok Dalwai Committee (2016) worked on Doubling Farmers' Income.
An MSP committee under Sanjay Agrawal was set up in July 2022.
The Essential Commodities Act dates from 1955.
e-NAM was launched on 14 April 2016 with SFAC as lead agency.
e-NAM is a pan-India electronic trading portal giving farmers nationwide markets (UPSC 2017).
Model APLM Act 2017 and Model Contract Farming Act 2018 were templates for States.
The three 2020 farm laws were repealed by the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021.
Seeds Act 1966; PPV&FR Act 2001; National Seeds Policy 2002.
The National Seeds Policy 2002 addresses the low seed replacement rate.
Nutrient Based Subsidy began in 2010 for P and K fertilisers; urea is excluded.
New Urea Policy 2015; neem-coated urea made 100% mandatory in 2015.
IFFCO nano urea was launched in 2021; first plant at Kalol, Gujarat.
One Nation One Fertiliser (2022) uses the single brand 'Bharat'.
PM-PRANAM (2023) rewards States that cut chemical-fertiliser use.
BPKP promotes chemical-free natural farming; PKVY promotes cluster organic farming.
The National Mission on Natural Farming was approved on 25 November 2024 with ₹2,481 crore.
Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic state in 2016.
PMKSY (2015) means 'Har Khet Ko Pani' and 'Per Drop More Crop'.
The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan.
The National Food Security Mission was launched in 2007.
PM-KUSUM (2019) promotes solar-powered irrigation pumps.
Soil Health Cards give a nutrient-status advisory for each field.
NABARD (1982) is the apex refinancing body for rural credit.
CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman, 1979) recommended NABARD, set up on 12 July 1982.
The All India Rural Credit Survey (A.D. Gorwala, 1951-54) led to the State Bank of India (1955).
The R.V. Gupta Committee (1998) led to the Kisan Credit Card.
The Vaidyanathan Committee (2004) dealt with reviving cooperative credit.
Short-term cooperative credit is three-tier: PACS, DCCB, StCB.
Commercial banks give the largest share of institutional farm credit.
Crop loans at 7% with a 3% prompt-repayment incentive give an effective 4%.
Budget 2025-26 raised the KCC limit under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme to ₹5 lakh.
KCC short-term credit covers working capital for farm-asset maintenance, post-harvest expenses and consumption (UPSC 2020).
Computerisation of PACS, social capital and government cold storage are public investment in agriculture (UPSC 2020).
PMFBY farmer premium: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi, 5% commercial/horticultural.
PMFBY is voluntary even for loanee farmers since 2020.
PMFBY was launched on 18 February 2016 at Sehore, replacing NAIS and MNAIS.
PMFBY covers post-harvest losses from cyclones and unseasonal rain (UPSC 2016).
From Kharif 2026 PMFBY covers wild animal attacks and paddy inundation.
PM-KISAN gives ₹6,000 a year in three instalments via DBT.
PM-KISAN was launched on 24 February 2019 at Gorakhpur.
The 23rd PM-KISAN instalment was released in June 2026.
PM-KISAN was extended from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with ₹3.15 lakh crore (Cabinet, 31 July 2026).
PM Kisan Maan Dhan gives a ₹3,000/month pension after 60.
PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (July 2025) covers 100 districts with ₹24,000 crore a year for 6 years.
PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana converges 36 schemes.
The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses (Oct 2025) has ₹11,440 crore for 2025-26 to 2030-31.
The pulses mission focuses on tur, urad and masoor.
The National Mission on Edible Oils — Oilseeds (Oct 2024) has ₹10,103 crore.
NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with ₹11,040 crore.
The Digital Agriculture Mission (Sep 2024, ₹2,817 crore) builds AgriStack farmer IDs.
FAO food-security dimensions: Availability, Accessibility, Utilization, Stability.
NFSA: 5 kg/person/month for priority households, 35 kg/household for AAY.
NFSA covers up to 75% rural and 50% urban people — about two-thirds (~81 crore).
Under NFSA the eldest woman aged 18+ is head of household for the ration card (UPSC 2018).
Pregnant and lactating women get a take-home ration and ₹6,000 maternity benefit under NFSA.
NFSA prices were ₹3 rice, ₹2 wheat and ₹1 millets per kg.
PMGKAY grain is free from 1 January 2023 and extended five years from 1 January 2024 for about 81.35 crore.
One Nation One Ration Card makes ration cards portable for migrants.
Revamped PDS began in 1992 for remote areas.
Targeted PDS began in 1997 with BPL/APL two-tier pricing.
Antyodaya Anna Yojana began in 2000 for the poorest families.
Fortified rice began as a 2019 pilot in 15 districts of 11 states.
ICDS began in 1975; the Mid-Day Meal became PM POSHAN in 2021.
Global Hunger Index 2025: India 102nd of 123.
NFHS-5: 35.5% of under-five children are stunted.
About 195 million Indians are undernourished (FAO).
Agriculture is about 18% of India's greenhouse-gas emissions.
FCI holds the buffer stock and procures at MSP.
ICAR was set up in 1929.
FCI was set up in 1965 under the Food Corporations Act, 1964.
NAFED dates from 1958 and CCI from 1970.
APEDA dates from 1986 and MPEDA from 1972 (Kochi).
Central Warehousing Corporation 1957; WDRA 2010.
ICRISAT (1972) is at Patancheru near Hyderabad.
Tea Board Kolkata, Coffee Board Bengaluru, Rubber Board Kottayam, Spices Board Kochi.
The Tobacco Board is headquartered at Guntur.
The Central Tobacco Research Institute is at Rajahmundry.
The Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is at Pedavegi, AP.
ANGRAU is at Lam, Guntur; Dr YSR Horticultural University at Venkataramannagudem.
AP is the largest shrimp producer in India (~70%).
AP ranks first in area and production of oil palm and papaya.
Rice is AP’s major crop, irrigated by the Krishna and Godavari rivers.
Polavaram is a multipurpose national project on the Godavari, targeted before the 2027 Pushkarams.
Pattiseema lifts Godavari water to the Krishna delta, linking the two rivers.
Handri-Neeva and Galeru-Nagari serve drought-prone Rayalaseema.
Veligonda Phase-1 was directed to be completed by mid-2026.
The Godavari-Banakacherla link is only proposed, under scrutiny.
Annadata Sukhibhava was allocated about ₹6,600 crore in the 2026-27 AP budget.
Annadata Sukhibhava gives ₹20,000 a year (₹14,000 State + ₹6,000 PM-KISAN).
Annadata Sukhibhava was launched on 2 August 2025 at Darsi (Prakasam) for about 46.86 lakh farmers.
AP agriculture budget 2026-27 (K. Atchannaidu) was about ₹53,753 crore.
Rythu Bharosa Kendras were renamed Rythu Seva Kendras in 2024.
RBKs are village one-stop centres for seeds, fertilisers, advice and procurement.
APCNF won the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024 and the Food Planet Prize 2026.
APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.
Agriculture and allied sectors are about 37% of AP's GSDP (2024-25).
AP leads India in eggs and fish.
Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest chilli market.
Banganapalle mango and Araku coffee have GI tags.
